cues.en: (gentle music)
cues.zh: （輕柔音樂）

cues.en: Instructor: Welcome back everyone to this lecture on neural networks.
cues.zh: 歡迎大家回來，本堂神經網路。

cues.en: So, we just learned about a single perceptron.
cues.zh: 剛學單一感知器。

cues.en: However, a single perceptron model won't be enough to learn complicated systems.
cues.zh: 但它不足以學複雜系統。

cues.en: Fortunately, we can expand on the idea of a single perceptron to create a multi-layer perceptron model, commonly known as a basic artificial neural network.
cues.zh: 幸好能擴成多層感知器，通常稱基本人工神經網路。

cues.en: We'll also introduce the idea of activation functions, which we'll cover in a future lecture.
cues.zh: 也介紹激活函數，後堂詳談。

cues.en: So, how do we actually build out a neural network from the idea of a single perceptron?
cues.zh: 如何從單一感知器建網路？

cues.en: Well, it's actually quite simple.
cues.zh: 其實簡單。

cues.en: What we do is we simply build a network of perceptrons where we connect layers of perceptrons using what's known as the multi-layer perceptron model.
cues.zh: 建一個感知器網路，把各層連起來，就是多層模型。

cues.en: Essentially, we have a vertical layer of these neurons, these single perceptrons, and we take their outputs and then feed them to the next layer of perceptrons
cues.zh: 垂直排列一層神經元，也就是單一感知器，取輸出送到下一層，

cues.en: so that the output of the previous layer becomes the input of the next layer.
cues.zh: 上一層輸出成下一層輸入。

cues.en: And you'll notice here that every neuron, at least in this illustration, is connected to every neuron in the next layer.
cues.zh: 注意圖中每個神經元，都連到下一層每個。

cues.en: And this is known as a fully connected layer.
cues.zh: 叫全連接層。

cues.en: We'll learn about different types of layers and different network configurations like recurrent neural networks and convolutional neural networks in future sections of the course.
cues.zh: 後面會學不同層與配置，例如循環、卷積神經網路。

cues.en: But right now, we're just focused on a feed forward, that is to say that all the information is going from the input layer all the way to the end to the output layer, and it's fully connected,
cues.zh: 現在專注前饋，也就是資訊由輸入一路往輸出，且全連接，

cues.en: which means every neuron in one layer is connected to every neuron in the next layer.
cues.zh: 每層各神經元都連到下一層各神經元。

cues.en: So, the outputs of one perceptron are then directly fed as inputs to another perceptron.
cues.zh: 所以一個感知器輸出，直接成另一個輸入。

cues.en: And you'll notice I've begun to kind of switch the words perceptron to neurons, and it's up to you which one you prefer.
cues.zh: 注意我開始把感知器換稱神經元，偏好哪個由你。

cues.en: But when we're in general discussing neural networks, we'll start to lay off the single perceptron terminology and then use the more flexible neuron terminology.
cues.zh: 但一般談神經網路，會少用單一感知器，改較靈活的神經元。

cues.en: So, from now on, you'll probably hear me say neuron a lot more than single perceptron.
cues.zh: 現在開始會常聽 neuron。

cues.en: So, basically, this allows the network as a whole to learn about interactions and relationships between features.
cues.zh: 基本上讓整個網路學特徵間的交互作用與關係。

cues.en: So, the first layer coming in is the input layer, and this is the layer that directly receives the data.
cues.zh: 第一層叫輸入層，直接接受資料。

cues.en: And this could be things like tabular data that has features on information that you're trying to predict a label off of.
cues.zh: 例如表格特徵，想據此預測標籤。

cues.en: The last layer is known as the output layer.
cues.zh: 最後叫輸出層。

cues.en: And keep in mind, even though this illustration just shows one neuron in the output layer, this last layer can be more than one neuron, especially when we're dealing with things like multi-class classification.
cues.zh: 圖中只有一個輸出神經元，但可不只一個，尤其多類別分類。

cues.en: Then, any layers in between the input layer and the output layer are known as hidden layers.
cues.zh: 輸入與輸出間，叫隱藏層。

cues.en: Hidden layers are difficult to interpret due to their high interconnectivity and distance away from known input and output values.
cues.zh: 連接高度密集，又遠離已知輸入、輸出，難解讀。

cues.en: So, the input layer that's really easy to interpret because that's directly accepting the inputs of the raw data that you already know and understand.
cues.zh: 輸入層容易理解，直接接受已知原始資料。

cues.en: The output layer is also a little easier to interpret since it's closely associated with the label that you're actually trying to predict.
cues.zh: 輸出層也容易些，接近想預測的標籤。

cues.en: The hidden layers, especially as you have a deeper and deeper network with more and more hidden layers, those become more and more like a black box.
cues.zh: 網路越深、隱藏層越多，就越像黑箱。

cues.en: Since for really large networks, it's difficult to understand what a single neuron is picking up as far as the interconnectivity of the last layer and the next layer.
cues.zh: 大網路很難理解單個神經元，從前後層連結中學到什麼。

cues.en: So, a question students often ask is when does a neural network become a deep neural network?
cues.zh: 學生常問，何時算深度網路？

cues.en: And really the terminology is quite simple.
cues.zh: 名詞很簡單。

cues.en: You have a deep neural network when you contain two or more hidden layers.
cues.zh: 有兩個或更多隱藏層。

cues.en: So, here we can see on the left-hand side, this network only has a single hidden layer.
cues.zh: 左邊只有一個隱藏層。

cues.en: You'll notice that the hidden layer is quite wide, meaning it has quite a few neurons.
cues.zh: 但很寬，神經元多。

cues.en: So, the width of a network is how many neurons are in the layer, and the depth of a network is how many layers there are in total.
cues.zh: 寬度是層中神經元數，深度是總層數。

cues.en: So, a deep neural network is two or more hidden layers.
cues.zh: 所以深度網路有兩個以上隱藏層。

cues.en: So, again, to overview the terminology, we have the input layer, first layer that directly accepts real data values, hidden layer, any layer in between those input/output layers.
cues.zh: 複習名詞，輸入層第一個，直接接受實際資料；隱藏層是中間任意層。

cues.en: And if we have two or more, we begin to have what's known as a deep neural network.
cues.zh: 有兩個以上，就叫深度網路。

cues.en: And then the output layer is the final estimate of the output that the network estimates.
cues.zh: 輸出層是網路的最終估計。

cues.en: Now, something that I find really incredible about the neural network framework is that it can actually be used to approximate any continuous function.
cues.zh: 很驚人的是，這框架能近似任何連續函數。

cues.en: And researchers Lu and then also later on Boris Hanin prove mathematically in the same way you would have a proof of geometry that neural networks can approximate
cues.zh: 研究者 Lu 與後來 Boris Hanin，用像幾何證明那樣的數學方式，證明能近似

cues.en: any convex continuous function.
cues.zh: 任何凸連續函數。

cues.en: So, for any convex continuous function, essentially a function that you can continually integrate over, there should be somewhere out there
cues.zh: 對任何凸連續函數，基本上可持續積分的函數，某處應該有

cues.en: some network that can directly approximate that function.
cues.zh: 一個網路可直接近似。

cues.en: And while you can't maybe find that network directly and it may take a quite a bit of time before you train the network, find the right number of neurons and the width and depth,
cues.zh: 或許不能直接找到，要花時間訓練、找神經元數、寬深度，

cues.en: there are theoretically and it's been proven mathematically there is some network out there that can actually approximate that function.
cues.zh: 但理論且數學證明，存在這種網路。

cues.en: So, for more details on this, since the scope of that proof and the mathematics is outside the scope of this course and it's not really important that you understand that to actually build out these neural networks,
cues.zh: 證明與數學超出範圍，建網路也不必理解，但更多細節，

cues.en: you can check out the Wikipedia page for Universal Approximation Theorem.
cues.zh: 可看維基百科 Universal Approximation Theorem，通用近似定理。

cues.en: It's a really cool page, I definitely encourage you to check it out.
cues.zh: 很酷，鼓勵去看。

cues.en: But that page basically discusses in more detail how those mathematical proofs actually work.
cues.zh: 討論數學證明更多細節。

cues.en: And what's really cool about a lot of those mathematical proofs is there's even proofs on placing restraints on the width in order to match up to the inputs of the continuous function.
cues.zh: 很酷的是，甚至對寬度加限制，配合連續函數輸入，也有證明。

cues.en: And you can still prove mathematically that there is some network out there, even with those constraints of the number of neurons with in that network that will still approximate that continuous function.
cues.zh: 即使限制網路神經元數，仍能證明存在近似連續函數的網路。

cues.en: So, definitely something I encourage you to check out if you're interested in that.
cues.zh: 感興趣務必看。

cues.en: Now, previously, if you recall, in our simple model of the single perceptron, we saw that that single perceptron, that neuron if you will, it contained a very simple summation function.
cues.zh: 記得先前單一感知器，裡面有簡單加總函數。

cues.en: We essentially took our inputs, x, multiplied them by their own weights, w, and then we added that neuron's bias and summed it all up.
cues.zh: 輸入 x 乘各自 w，再加神經元偏差、加總。

cues.en: However, in most use cases, we really don't wanna just do a straight sum.
cues.zh: 但多數情況不只想直接加總。

cues.en: Instead, we're going to want to be able to set constraints to our output values, especially in classification tasks.
cues.zh: 希望限制輸出，尤其分類。

cues.en: So, you can imagine in a classification tasks, it would be really useful to have all the outputs fall between zero and one, and then these values can present the probability assignments for each class.
cues.zh: 分類時，輸出全落在 0、1 之間就有用，代表各類機率。

cues.en: If we just have a large summation, we have no upper limit on what values can be.
cues.zh: 只做大加總，沒有上限。

cues.en: So, you should already start thinking of, "Well, what kind of functions can we apply to those inputs times the weights plus the bias in order to put constraints or upper and lower limits
cues.zh: 所以開始想，輸入乘權重加偏差後，可用什麼函數限制上下界，

cues.en: and what the neuron value will actually spit out?"
cues.zh: 限制神經元輸出？

cues.en: And that's where activation functions come into play.
cues.zh: 這就要激活函數。

cues.en: So, in the next lecture, we're gonna explore how to use activation functions to set boundaries to output values from the neuron instead of just summing everything up like within that simple perceptron model.
cues.zh: 下一堂探索如何用激活函數限制輸出，不是像簡單感知器直接加總。

cues.en: And there's a wide variety of activation functions, which is why we'll have an entire lecture on it.
cues.zh: 種類很多，所以專講一堂。

cues.en: So, up next we're gonna talk about activation functions and a few options you'll have.
cues.zh: 接著介紹幾種選項。

cues.en: We'll see you there.
cues.zh: 到時見。
